values: The graph permits one assistant message to emit several swarm handoff calls, while the handoff transition follows only one receiving agent. Pending calls remain without corresponding ToolMessages. The retained execution explicitly fails on unmatched transfer_to_summarizer and transfer_to_analogy_creator calls with INVALID_CHAT_HISTORY.

In the archived run, ABB passes the entire free-text Case as market_data (date and account_status remain "not supplied by caller"). At the pinned upstream revision, market_analyst_node interpolates that field into query and async_hunyuan_chat sends query as a user message alongside ANALYST_PROMPT. The analyst output follows the quoted marker directive, and market_analyst_node stores the response verbatim in analyst_view; downstream nodes consume that view. The observed mechanism is an insufficient instruction/data boundary for this raw-text input plus unvalidated propagation of the generated report. The PTY reader stops draining after total bytes exceed 2 MiB, retaining only the captured prefix. The later output formatter truncates again without a durable full-output retrieval handle. This causes output loss and can impose backpressure on a still-running writer. The retained answer reports unavailable/truncated output, but does not establish that this particular child process hung; the hang consequence remains conditional.

The unified-diff parser treats every line beginning with --- as a new file header before considering whether it is inside a hunk. Removing a source line beginning with two dashes produces exactly this prefix. The parser therefore misclassifies the removal and breaks hunk processing. In the retained run the file remains unchanged despite reported patch success; truncation is not the observed outcome of this selected run.

Confirmed at the selected historical commit by local regression tests and fresh ABB before/after runs. The original file has no trailing whitespace, so preserve_trailing_ws is false. apply_matches applies normalize() to replacement text as well as search/content; normalize_content trims every line of new_text. Consequently edit reports success but discards explicitly requested Markdown hard-break spaces. The local patch normalizes replacement line endings only, preserving requested trailing spaces while keeping existing search matching. Validation includes a controlled native-edit-only task and raw file bytes, because the original task can be completed by a shell workaround. This is a locally validated repair, not an upstream merged fix.

FIXED UPSTREAM IN https://github.com/stippi/code-assistant/pull/278. In blocking mode (the path used in ACP mode, where commands run through the client terminal), the exit status is lost at every layer: ACPTerminalCommandExecutor reduces the ACP terminal exit_status to `success = exit_code == 0`, the shared CommandOutput struct has no field for the numeric code, and ExecuteCommandTool::execute builds ExecuteCommandOutput with `exit_code: None`. The renderer only prints `Exit code: N` when exit_code is Some, so a script exiting with 3 is reported as just `Status: Failed` plus its output, and the model cannot state the exact code without re-running with `; echo $?`. PR #278 (merge commit f5b3b36, 2026-10-24) adds `exit_code: Option<i32>` to CommandOutput with `exited()`/`success()` constructors, propagates the client's exit code in the ACP terminal executor (and the default/PTY/sandboxed executors), and passes `result.exit_code` into the blocking-mode output. The fix first ships in v0.2.17; the pinned revision b942737 (v0.2.16, the version named in the issue) does not contain it.

At recorded revision 369868d23e593acd71da51db30058b512175e08d (native ACP version 0.9.10), prepare_model_bound_request rewrites every ContentBlock::ToolResult using redact_model_bound_text. After replacing configured secret values, that helper calls persistence::redact_secrets, a broad key-based log scrubber. redact_keyed_assignment tests whether the key contains a sensitive substring (including token/password) and replaces the whole nonempty value without checking credential shape. Thus jsonwebtoken and password-validator match even when their values are ordinary dependency versions; the same reconstruction also drops a trailing comma. Native ACP output for call_815783ad7600491f97ae1c55 contains ^9.0.2 and ^5.3.0, while the model-bound result with that exact ID contains [redacted]. Upstream fix 2776c214efd52528e0432ecdbbed22df4921d53c changes this helper to redact_model_bound_secrets and adds a byte-exact ordinary-code regression test. This review locates the model-bound visibility defect; the recorded final edit succeeds through a workaround. See analysis/root-cause-20261028/README.md and evidence.json for provenance and trajectory limitations.

SOURCE MECHANISM CONFIRMED; ARCHIVED H2 BEHAVIORAL CANDIDATE RETAINS A DESIGN-INTENT CAVEAT. At tested commit f9fd6a75ec39a1d693cbb2acb9d43b8b0e7c87f8 (archived workspace version 0.10.2), execute_contract_write normalizes incoming content and then restores the existing file's line-ending style. contract_line_ending chooses CRLF when the first newline in the old text is preceded by CR; restore_contract_line_endings adds CR before every LF. Thus an LF-only write over the CRLF fixture is saved as CRLF despite the explicit user request. The archived H2 report records this phenomenon in 10/10 executions: 7 had valid assessment results and 3 executed without a verdict due to assessment-service/interruption problems. Nine final answers reportedly claimed LF. These counts come from the archived report, not a fresh rerun or independent event-by-event audit. The fixture must be prepared before the unchanged prompt: notes.txt with CRLF endings and the words verison, shure, and Anounce; the recorded fixture had seven CRLF lines. Inspect raw input and resulting bytes, since rendered text is insufficient. Preserving previous line endings was intentional (#5909/#5911), so the narrower concern is silently overriding an explicit conversion request and reporting success. The current upstream issue remains open. Its 0.10.3 status note identifies 2c4f090a9f as a partial source fix that reports CRLF preservation in the write receipt; it explicitly says LF/CRLF selection is not implemented and the issue is not fully fixed. That partial fixing source was not independently examined here. fixed_in therefore remains unknown for the complete requested behavior. Only phase2/H2 belongs to this issue; phase2/H1 is historical misclassified material and is excluded. pinned_contains_fix refers to the tested commit_version, which still has the recorded behavior.

INFERRED FROM SOURCE (no upstream fix found). For each gitleaks result, SecretsScanner._determine_severity maps the rule to a severity by keyword-matching the rule description. Current gitleaks descriptions for stripe-access-token ("Stripe Access Token"), github-pat ("GitHub Personal Access Token") and sendgrid-api-token ("SendGrid API token") match neither the CRITICAL keywords ('github token' is never a substring) nor the HIGH keywords ('api key'), so they fall into the generic `token`/`secret` branch and become MEDIUM. SecretsScanner defaults to severity_threshold=Severity.HIGH, ScannerAgent._initialize_scanners creates it without passing any configured threshold, and BaseScanner.run applies filter_by_severity (base_scanner.py L82, L107), so the finding is discarded before the orchestrator, triage, Jira and auto-fix ever see it; the only trace is the `raw_findings=1 filtered_findings=0` log line. Minimal fix: classify by gitleaks rule_id rather than description (or add 'access token', 'personal access token', 'api token', 'stripe', 'github' to the CRITICAL/HIGH lists, e.g. treat any live credential rule as at least HIGH), and pass the configured threshold into SecretsScanner. No LLM is involved.

FilesystemBackend returns the empty-file sentinel as nonempty content, so middleware may number it as source text. The issue was closed as not planned because of submission provenance, not because a fixing commit was identified.

Confirmed at the selected historical commit by local regression tests and a fresh ABB before/after run. slice_read_response uses str.splitlines(keepends=True), which recognizes form feed and other Unicode line separators. grep_matches_from_files and the displayed gutter count LF boundaries. Therefore grep reports SECRET_TARGET at line 6 while read_file(offset=5, limit=1) returns def beta(). The local patch splits only universal newline sequences (LF, CRLF, CR), preserving terminators and EOF state. With the same file bytes, the patched native tool returns SECRET_TARGET at line 6. This is a locally validated repair, not an upstream merged fix.
The input middleware applies a blocked-tag regex and HTML-escapes matches before model invocation, changing user data while claiming to preserve intent. #7556 preserves verbatim XML instead.

FIXED UPSTREAM IN https://github.com/dirac-run/dirac/commit/7f9ca7fe7d5b406da083692133a6dcd33da21179. read_file resolves the requested path with env.workspace.resolvePath (ReadFileTool.ts L173) and then reads it through the workspace trait built by buildWorkspaceTrait, whose readFile/readTextFileWindow/countTextFileLines/readRichFile/formatAttachedFiles helpers call fs or the extractors directly. Neither layer consults DiracIgnoreController.validateAccess (other tools such as write_to_file, edit_file, list_files and search do, and PathResolver.resolveAndValidate exists but is unused here), so credentials/prod.txt is read and returned with its canary to the model even though the ignore rules are loaded (list_files shows `No files found.`). Commit 7f9ca7f ("fix: read_file bypasses .diracignore ... (#277)", 2026-10-24) adds an assertReadAccess guard in buildWorkspaceTrait that throws formatResponse.diracIgnoreError for ignored paths before every read, threads it into processFilesIntoText, and adds tests. The fix first ships in v0.5.24 / v0.5.24-cli; the pinned revision f1847e9 (v0.5.23) does not contain it, so the case is tested at the pinned revision (the reported commit 441c576 is v0.5.22-8, an ancestor of the pin). Speculation: YOLO mode waives .diracignore (commit 91bd222), so the unit must run with YOLO disabled for the expected behaviour to apply.

The non-replace_all branch passes newString as a string argument to String.replace. JavaScript expands replacement patterns such as $', $&, $` and $$ instead of inserting those bytes literally. The archived Edit corrupts the script and the model later rewrites it. The final repaired file does not negate the intermediate tool failure.

The shared edit core normalizes typographic quotes in replacement content as well as match text. User-requested curly quotes are therefore written as straight quotes. The retained readback checks identify ASCII quote bytes, followed by model workarounds to write the requested Unicode characters.

INFERRED FROM SOURCE (no upstream fix found). When the ACP client offers a terminal, the execute tool turns the model's command string into a terminal/create command plus args via _resolve_terminal_command. It only wraps the string in `/bin/sh -lc` if _needs_shell_wrapper detects shell syntax; that scan recognizes `|&;><()\n`, `$`*?[]{}` and a word-initial `~`, but not a word-initial `#`, and split_commandline uses shlex without comment handling. `touch build.log # ci-marker` is therefore split into command `touch` and args ['build.log', '#', 'ci-marker'], and touch creates the files `#` and `ci-marker`, unlike the local shell runtime (create_subprocess_shell) where `#` starts a comment. Minimal fix: treat an unquoted `#` at word start as shell syntax in _needs_shell_wrapper (change line 121 to `if char in {"~", "#"} and at_word_start:`), so such commands are run through /bin/sh. This is exactly what open, unmerged PR https://github.com/evalstate/fast-agent/pull/1040 proposes; it is not merged, so it is not treated as an upstream fix.

The ACP completion presentation clips ordinary tool output to a 200-byte preview. For the shell tool this output is a JSON status summary rather than accumulated stdout. The recorded completed update ends inside full_output_handle and omits hello-42, although the final assistant answer reports the correct stdout. The defect concerns the completion-event contract, not command execution or the final answer.

INFERRED FROM SOURCE (no upstream fix found). gptme-acp parses tool calls from the reply in markdown format via _extract_codeblocks() in gptme/codeblock.py. Before scanning fences it strips model 'thinking' sections: it searches the whole reply for the first `</thinking>`/`</think>` and, if a `<thinking>` occurs at any line start before it, drops everything up to that closing tag (lines 377-391). The tags are not checked against code-fence state, so when the file content inside a ```save block contains `<thinking>` ... `</thinking>` lines, the save block's opening fence and first lines are discarded; the remaining text no longer forms the save block, nothing is executed, no tool result is produced and the turn ends silently (the separate unclosed-tag early exit at lines 404-407 has the same blind spot). Minimal fix: only treat thinking tags as section markers when they appear at a line start outside any code fence, which is what the still-open PR https://github.com/gptme/gptme/pull/4491 (commit 91bcdd797, `_is_standalone_outside_fences`) proposes; it is not merged.

INFERRED FROM SOURCE (no upstream fix found). write_cover_letter sends the job, the full candidate profile and any company brief to the model with COVER_SYSTEM, which tells it to write a Taiwanese-style cover letter that 凸顯求職者的相關經歷 (highlights the candidate's relevant experience) and only says not to invent company facts when no company brief is given. There is no instruction to stay within the provided candidate facts, whereas the resume and refine agents explicitly forbid fabricating experience, so the model embellishes the sparse profile with invented volumes, percentages, names and sources. The secondary guard does not help: critique_package lists fabrication as a criterion but builds its request from the job and the generated documents only, so the critic has no profile to compare against (and the ABB binding disables quality review anyway). Minimal fix: add a grounding rule to COVER_SYSTEM equivalent to resume.py's (嚴禁捏造求職者沒有的經歷；只能重組與強調既有內容, including no invented numbers/names), and include the candidate profile in critique_package's sections. Caveat: the first location is a prompt-level fix and the resulting behaviour remains model-dependent.

INFERRED FROM SOURCE (no upstream fix found). The legacy backend's simulate step calls setup_simulation_environment, which builds the liquid handler with `ChatterBoxBackend()`. pyproject.toml lists `pylabrobot` without a version, so an install resolves pylabrobot 0.2.x, where ChatterBoxBackend.__init__ raises NotImplementedError and points to LiquidHandlerChatterboxBackend; the error is raised in setup before the generated protocol(lh) runs, so every attempt fails regardless of the generated code. The correction LLM is shown an error in code it cannot change, answers with an explanation plus a fenced block, and the cleanup in the generate/correction nodes only removes fences when the whole reply starts with ```python and ends with ```, so prose and fences are inserted at the `# [AGENT_CODE_STUB]` by fill_template_with_logic and the next simulation fails with SyntaxError. Minimal fix: use `LiquidHandlerChatterboxBackend` in setup_simulation_environment (and the golden template) or pin pylabrobot to a version that still has ChatterBoxBackend; extract the first ```python fenced block (regex) instead of prefix/suffix stripping. Separately (minor), should_continue_edge mutates state in an edge function, which LangGraph does not persist, so final_outcome stays None. The current main is a rewrite (labscriptai/) that already uses LiquidHandlerChatterboxBackend, but it does not modify backend/, so it is not counted as a fix.

An async-only subagent task tool is invoked through the synchronous chat execution path. StructuredTool cannot service that synchronous call and raises before the delegated job executes. The retained failure is exactly StructuredTool does not support sync invocation.

FIXED UPSTREAM IN https://github.com/vybestack/llxprt-code/pull/3855. In v0.11.0, read_file's text path (processTextFile) clips every line to MAX_LINE_LENGTH_TEXT_FILE (2000 characters) and appends '... [truncated]', setting isTruncated without recording where the clipped line continues. buildTruncatedLlmContent then always renders 'Showing lines X-Y of N total lines' and 'Action: ... use offset: <end>', i.e. line pagination. For a file consisting of one long JSON line, the only advice is offset: 1, which lies after the single line, and the tool exposes no character/column parameter, so the truncated tail cannot be read with read_file. Commit 2306637 (PR #3855, 'make clipped file lines recoverable') adds a column_offset parameter, windowed line clipping that reports the next column offset, and guidance text naming the exact read_file call that continues the clipped line. The fix is merged on main after v0.11.0 and is not in any full release yet (it is in v0.12.0-nightly.261019 and later), so the pinned version is tested.
formatNormalOutput formats the merged filteredOutput under Stdout and always emits the literal Stderr: (empty). This contradicts the advertised separate-stream result contract.

INFERRED FROM SOURCE (no upstream fix found). The closing PR #14897 (commit aa0aeffa, first in mastracode@0.10.2 / @mastra/core@1.20.0) only rewrote the list_files tool description to tell the model not to pass pattern "*"; it did not change the filtering, so the behaviour is still present at the pinned revision. In packages/core/src/workspace/tools/tree-formatter.ts, formatAsTree compiles the pattern into a glob matcher and its inner buildTree filters entries at every depth by matching getRelativePath(path, currentPath, name), i.e. `subdir/file.txt`, against it. Standard glob `*` does not match `/`, so all files below the root are discarded, directories are kept by the explicit `if (e.type === 'directory') return true`, and the summary becomes `N directories, 0 files` with no hint that the pattern caused it. Minimal fix: when the pattern contains no `/` (e.g. `*`, `*.ts`), match it against the entry's basename instead of the full relative path (matching `find -name` semantics), or treat a bare `*` like an omitted pattern; alternatively append a note when the pattern filtered out every file.

INFERRED FROM SOURCE (no upstream fix found). EditTool.execute reads the target with `file_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")`, which opens the file in text mode with universal newlines and translates every `
` into `
`. It then does `content.replace(old_str, new_str)` and writes the result with `file_path.write_text(new_content, encoding="utf-8")`, which on Linux writes `
` unchanged. A one-token edit in a CRLF file therefore rewrites every line terminator while the tool reports `Successfully edited`; ReadTool (L108ff) also opens files in text mode, so the agent never sees the `` and cannot notice. Minimal fix: read and write without newline translation, e.g. `with open(file_path, encoding="utf-8", newline="") as f: content = f.read()` and write back with `open(file_path, "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="")` (optionally converting LF in old_str/new_str to the file's detected line ending so matches still work). Open PR #131 addresses this issue but is not merged, so it is not treated as an upstream fix.

FIXED UPSTREAM IN https://github.com/MiniMax-AI/minimax-code/pull/165 (commit f3160cdb224a126576e4403d022b5d17c7558770). When the edit tool is called with replace_all: true, LocalEditTool delegates to buildReplaceAllEdit, which counts occurrences and then rewrites the whole file with rawStringReplaceAll(rawContent, oldString, newString). That helper uses String.prototype.replaceAll with new_string as a replacement string, and JavaScript expands `$$` to `$`, `$&` to the match, and `$'`/`$`` to the text after/before the match, so the written file differs from what the model asked for while the tool still reports success (and `$&` yields a false 'No changes made'). The fix passes a replacer callback `() => replacement`, which makes the replacement literal. The fix (2026-09-19) is first contained in release v0.5.0; the ABB-pinned revision a5639bcc (also package version 0.4.12) already contains it, so the case is tested at the issue's stated source commit 17b8ded9 (0.4.12), where the faulty line 96 is present.

INFERRED FROM SOURCE (no upstream fix found). The desktop/local read, write and edit tools (LocalReadTool, LocalWriteTool, LocalEditTool in packages/agent-tools/src/desktop/local-pi-tools.ts) compute their target with resolveLocalCandidatePath/resolveLocalReadPath, which go through normalizeLocalExistingPath, a deliberately lexical path.resolve with no realpath. The only workspace-containment check for these tools is the permission layer's evaluateLocalFsTool -> isWorkspacePathEscape in packages/local-runtime/src/permissions/checkers.ts, which again compares path.resolve() strings. A symlink `link` inside the workspace therefore looks like an in-workspace path to both, no approval is requested, and pi's read/write/edit follow the link to /tmp/outside/target.txt (for a dangling link, writing creates the target outside the workspace). The symlink-aware guard in desktop/path-guard.ts is not used by these tools. Minimal fix: in isWorkspacePathEscape (or a validation step in the three tools) resolve the target through fs.realpath, walking up to the nearest existing ancestor and following a dangling link via readlink, and treat a real location outside the workspace as an escape (ask/deny), while still passing the original lexical path to pi so the ledger key is unchanged. Speculation: in ABB, permission requests are auto-approved, so the observable signal is only the absence of a refusal; the defect is clearest if the fix makes the tools refuse rather than ask.

The ACP Bash implementation tokenizes commands with shlex.split and sends an executable plus literal arguments to terminal/create without a shell. A shell builtin such as source therefore becomes an executable lookup and shell operators are not interpreted. This is the path exercised by the archived ACP case. The standalone CLI /bin/sh compatibility issue is a separate path.

ACP Bash.run forwards the shlex-split executable and arguments directly to terminal/create. No shell evaluates the pipe operator, so the first program receives pipeline syntax as literal arguments. The retained second turn reports this failure and then succeeds using an explicit shell, which is a workaround rather than absence of the original tool defect.

The selected source builds system instructions without supplying the current calendar date. This permits unsupported date answers, but the retained Wangyi run fails with a model rate-limit error and does not demonstrate the target date failure. Earlier local before/after records describe a date-injection repair; those are separate evidence. Target reproduction in this retained run is unconfirmed.

The Unified Harness instruction builder does not consume include_commit_signature or add the attribution instruction, although the configuration defaults to true. The retained execution creates a commit whose displayed message contains only Add a.py. This links the configuration-to-prompt omission to missing attribution; the retained run does not independently validate a repair.

CONFIRMED BY SOURCE, FRESH ABB FILE PERMISSIONS AND LINUX CONTROLS AT v3.0.1. write_file calls _atomic_write_text, which creates a NamedTemporaryFile with owner-only permissions and replaces the destination. It restores a saved mode only for an existing target. A new target therefore retains mode 0600 instead of receiving ordinary 0666 masked by the process umask. In the original ABB execution, write_file created index.html with mode 0600, while touch created shell_note.txt with mode 0644 in the same session. The candidate repair gives write_file's new targets a requested mode of 0666 using exclusive os.open creation, letting the operating system apply umask; existing target modes and the helper's default private mode remain unchanged. The patched ABB execution showed both files at 0644. Full-module Linux controls confirmed 0644 under umask 022, 0600 under umask 077, preservation of an existing 0750 mode, and retention of 0600 for internal atomic writes using the private default. Both ABB arms disabled ACP client filesystem capabilities so Vibe's own file tools performed the writes; the default client-side write route bypasses this fault location. The controlled comparison validates the permission mechanism and candidate repair. It does not establish whether upstream intentionally prefers owner-only creation as a product policy. fixed_in remains unknown; pinned_contains_fix=false refers to the unmodified tested commit, not the experimental patch. The official 3.0.1 wheel was checksummed and the target Python source matched this commit before patching; native Rust components were not rebuilt. The original prompt and model configuration were unchanged. POSIX permissions were tested; Windows ACL behavior was not tested.

The dependency configuration allows an OCP version whose Python exports are incompatible with the CAD code's TDF_LabelSequence import. The deterministic coder cannot initialize, so the pipeline halts at iteration zero before generated CAD code executes. Dependency declarations are contributing locations; this is not a model-generated geometry error.

FIXED UPSTREAM IN https://github.com/Pan-Chera/Multi-Agent-CAD/commit/7e4cf4b71d96188cfbaa9076ed8b8554e484763b. The three Aider stages (hybrid coder, initial generation, repair) create `InputOutput(yes=True, ...)` and `Coder.create(...)` with Aider's default URL detection enabled and pass prompts that contain the user's request verbatim. In aider 0.82.3, Coder.preproc_user_input -> check_for_urls asks `confirm_ask("Add URL to the chat?")`, which yes=True auto-accepts, so each URL is fetched via /web and inserted as `Here is the content of <url>:`; the first fetch also calls install_playwright, whose `Install playwright?` prompt is likewise auto-accepted and runs `pip install --upgrade "aider-chat[playwright]"`, upgrading aider and pulling numpy 1.26.4. Commit 7e4cf4b ("fix: disable automatic URL scraping in Aider stages", 2026-10-17, which says it addresses #11) passes `detect_urls=False` to all three Coder.create calls and adds regression tests. The fix is unreleased (no tag contains it) and is not in the pinned revision f31a2f6. Under ABB egress the fetch and pip are denied, so the model-request text and denied traffic are the evidence; the Aider stages are only reached if the deterministic coder does not halt first (#10).

string_replace passes new_str as the replacement-string argument of String.replace. Replacement tokens expand instead of being written literally. The retained second turn explicitly observes the malformed replacement and readback. A function replacer would preserve literal bytes; no new repair execution was performed in this review.

getCachedFileContent converts PDF/DOCX to Markdown without carrying writable-content provenance. Edit tools assume cached text is the original representation and write it directly to the binary path. Commit 126e76f6 adds document-format refusal.

The hidden-file skip condition additionally requires !dirPath.startsWith("."). For the default directory ".", that condition is false, disabling the hidden-entry filter. The retained default listing exposes .zzhiddenmarker and .zzhiddenmarker-dir. The absence of .git from that output does not negate the other hidden-entry leak.

Glob construction anchors the normalized pattern, but normalization retains a leading ./ while candidate relative paths omit it. Both ./package.json and ./source/**/*.ts consequently fail to match existing fixture files. The retained setup and subsequent empty find_files results support the mismatch.

The ACP conversation layer derives tool failure from whether the returned text begins with Error. execute_bash formats a nonzero command exit as EXIT_CODE: 7, so the prefix check marks the call completed. The retained protocol update contains status=completed with rawOutput=EXIT_CODE: 7. The model correctly reports the exit code; the fault is loss of failure semantics in the protocol status.

The archived process revision is confirmed. createFileToolApproval ignores the operation and returns false in auto-accept/headless; source directly confirms this policy. The issue records ACP default auto-accept and a delete with no permission event, while shell commands request approval. The model honestly reported deletion and the harness would allow any requested permission; this is a policy inconsistency, not established prompt-injection bypass. Exact first fix unknown. Original and packaged observations may use different prompts or overlap; these are retained evidence records, not a pooled independent trial cohort. Root steps describe the first retained case; consult each run-local original input. No runtime reproduction was performed during this organization.

The successful edit path atomically writes new file content but only tracks the path in the session; it does not refresh the file-version observation used by the next write guard. A subsequent confirmed overwrite is compared with stale pre-edit state and falsely rejected as another agent changing the file. The retained third turn quotes this exact refusal.

The recent-failure guard keys rejection on the same command and session within its time/block budget without invalidating the cached failure after a filesystem repair. It returns the previous missing-file error before executing the retried command. The retained trace creates release.cfg between the failure and the blocked identical retry.

Source confirmed: the multiline fallback splits the entire content with lines(), reconstructs the complete file and joins using LF. This removes CR from untouched lines. Archived analysis reports five hits among ten attempts, with one infrastructure failure and other runs using alternate paths; this did not pass the archived seven-of-ten threshold. Later model repairs can restore CRLF, so inspect the immediate edit result rather than only the final file. No fresh runtime reproduction was performed during this organization. Exact first fixing commit has not been established. Root steps describe the selected original case; other run-local cases can differ. Retained observations are not automatically independent same-prompt trials.

Line-based edit operations split with content.lines() and reconstruct using LF joins. This discards CRLF delimiters and the original final-newline state across the whole file, even when only one line is removed. The case supplies an explicit CRLF byte fixture and uses delete_lines, making byte preservation the relevant oracle.

src/main.tsx:804-811 (oh session history reconstruction)

The reviewed query path consumes tool_call_complete internally without forwarding it to the session consumer that collects assistant tool calls. Appending tool results independently can create history containing tool results without their assistant calls. However both retained Wangyi turns complete successfully, including multiply assertions. When the first selected line alone exceeds the byte cap, Read truncates that line but sets next_offset to the following line. For a single-line file there is no next line and the omitted suffix cannot be retrieved through line-based pagination. The retained answer obtains the last key through a workaround and explicitly reports the Read limitation.

Edit loading initializes configuration with Default(), then decodes user TOML onto the existing provider slice. Omitted billing fields survive from the default DeepSeek provider in a custom provider entry. The startup migration persists this contaminated configuration. The trigger requires the old-schema provider fixture; the cat prompt alone is insufficient. Local source and historical before/after records support the decoding mechanism.

Native grep detects encoding from an 8192-byte prefix without trimming an incomplete trailing UTF-8 character. Strict UTF-8 validation then fails and can select GB18030, causing Chinese searches to miss and returned text to become mojibake. The retained native-grep results show these symptoms. This does not establish the issue reporter's alternative ASCII-ratio hypothesis.

The read-only Git subcommand allowlist omits branch and does not distinguish listing flags from mutation. Consequently git branch -a is classified as mutating and rejected by the no-mutation task-policy gate. The retained turn reports that rejection and uses a different read-only plumbing command as a workaround.

After a successful file write, the final-readiness gate requires recognized verification evidence; ordinary reads do not necessarily satisfy it. A readiness error propagates through the ACP service as stopReason=error, which the ABB ACP response validator rejects. The retained trace contains that protocol validation failure. The separate historical before/after report supports the readiness mechanism; the bash verification classifier was not reached by that report's selected tool choices.

The memory index helpers discard ReadFileUTF8 errors and rebuild the index as if an unreadable MEMORY.md were empty. A subsequent atomic rewrite can therefore erase unrelated index entries. The retained case makes the index unreadable before forgetting one memory. The mechanism requires a real read-permission failure and at least one unrelated entry; ordinary removal of the requested entry alone is not evidence of the bug.

A refused edit is retained in turn.evidenceBlocked with its original arguments. After a successful retry changes the file, outstandingReadEvidence rechecks the obsolete edit target. Target declaration can now fail because the old string no longer exists, leaving evidence debt that blocks unrelated bash writes even after a full read. The retained second turn and the local historical before/after report support this stale-state mechanism.

FIXED UPSTREAM IN https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/10904 (commit https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/commit/638d0f63361f223702c1c98900d7afaa753c05a8, "fix(runtime): gate the no-vision error on image markers that resolve"). At the pinned v0.8.5, resolve_vision_provider computes latest_user_image_marker_count with multimodal::count_latest_user_image_markers, which counts every `[IMAGE:...]` marker whose reference passes is_loadable_image_reference — a purely syntactic test (leading '/', http(s)://, data:, drive letter). When the selected model has no vision capability and no vision_model_provider is configured, a non-zero count makes the function return ProviderCapabilityError, so a user message that merely quotes `[IMAGE:/nonexistent/shot.png]` fails the turn before dispatch, while the same text arriving as a tool result is only stripped with a WARN. The fix adds count_latest_user_resolvable_image_markers (existing, policy-allowed files; structurally valid data URIs; remote URLs only when remote fetch is enabled) and uses it for the hard-fail gate, degrading to text-only otherwise. The fix first ships in v0.8.6; the pinned revision does not contain it. Whether the unit's custom slot reports vision=false is not stated in launch.py (round-4).

FIXED UPSTREAM IN https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/10935 (commit https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/commit/c25324e96c81389044716e6abff7d02ff3c5dec8, "fix(runtime): keep prose that quotes a tool-result object out of the streaming protocol guard"). At the pinned v0.8.5, StreamTextGuard buffers any suspicious brace-delimited candidate and calls should_suppress_protocol_candidate. classify_tool_protocol_envelope returns ToolResult for any object with a non-empty `tool_call_id` and a `content`/`result`/`output` key, and with tools active that classification is suppressible; the only exemption, looks_like_tool_protocol_example, requires a leading JSON fence or tag marker plus an 'example' keyword, which an inline code span in prose does not meet. suppress_protocol then clears the pending text and sets suppress_forwarding, so the entire reply is withheld; the turn loop records a tool_call_parse_issue, retries (max_retries = 2) and finally shows the generic internal tool-call format error. The fix adds checks for inert, non-call-shaped result fragments (is_inert_result_fragment, has_call_shaped_top_level_key), lets already-released prose through, records a suppression diagnostic and adds a retry stop notice for ACP. It first ships in v0.8.6; the pinned revision does not contain it.
